claims.text: The 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces a coating with inadequate thickness.
Broadening the feedstock distribution from 15–45 μm to approximately 15–75 μm will increase deposited mass per pass.
The coarser-inclusive feedstock will produce a thicker coating than the 15–45 μm baseline.
The coarser-inclusive feedstock will allow the coating to meet the required thickness specification.
The intervention is to use a 15–75 μm feedstock while holding all other spray parameters constant.
Coarser particles have greater mass per particle.
Coarser particles impact with greater momentum.
Greater particle momentum produces thicker or larger splats.
Larger or thicker splats enhance layer build-up and deposition efficiency.
Coarser particles promote improved inter-splat bonding.
The lower specific surface area of coarser particles reduces their susceptibility to in-flight oxidation.
The coarser-inclusive feedstock will not detrimentally increase as-sprayed oxidation relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
The coarser-inclusive feedstock will preserve coating adhesion and integrity relative to the baseline.
The 15–45 μm baseline coating exhibits minimal oxidation and acceptable integrity.
The intervention should remain effective during subsequent aero-engine high-temperature cyclic service as a thermal-barrier-system bond coat.
The intervention is effective only if coarse particles avoid poor splat flattening, excessive in-flight deceleration, and splat nonuniformity.
The proposed experiment compares 15–45 μm and 15–75 μm feedstocks under otherwise identical thermal-spray and post-deposition conditions.
Failure to significantly increase or meet the required thickness, or an increase in oxidation or loss of integrity, will falsify the hypothesis.
